mainTopic: The ceremony of תקיעות on a public fast, the חכמים limiting it to the מקדש, and the dispute between רבי יהושע and חכמים about how the כהנים of the משמר and the בית אב fast.
overview: The amud opens with the end of a משנה. It finishes a story from the days of רבי חלפתא and רבי חנניא בן תרדיון, who ran a fast-day service with shofar blasts and 'מי שענה' prayers in place of אמן, as was done in the מקדש. The חכמים say this ceremony belongs only at the שער מזרח and the הר הבית. A new משנה follows. In it, רבי יהושע and חכמים disagree on how strictly the אנשי משמר and the אנשי בית אב fast in each set of public fasts. The משנה then gives their rules on wine, haircuts and laundry. It also covers the days listed in מגילת תענית, which weekday a series of fasts may start on, and fasts that fall on ראש חודש, חנוכה or פורים. Then the גמרא begins. It limits the ark-and-ashes ceremony to the final seven fasts, and explains why the leaders receive ashes first. Finally, רבי אבא דמן קסרי starts to explain why someone else places the ashes on the leaders' heads, and his answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The fast-day ceremony in the days of רבי חלפתא
steps.stepSummary: The משנה tells how, in the days of רבי חלפתא and רבי חנניא בן תרדיון, the prayer leader finished each blessing. Instead of answering אמן, the people heard a call for the כהנים to blow the shofar, followed by a 'He Who answered' formula.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the days of רבי חלפתא and רבי חנניא בן תרדיון, someone led the prayers in front of the ark and finished the whole blessing, but the people did not answer 'amen' after him. Instead, a call went out: 'Blow, כהנים, blow!' Then the leader said: 'He Who answered אברהם אבינו on הר המוריה will answer you and hear your cry today.' Then the call came again: 'Blast, sons of אהרן, blast!' And the leader said: 'He Who answered our fathers at ים סוף will answer you and hear your cry today.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is finishing a story. It describes a special fast-day ceremony that was held in the town of these two rabbis.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a congregation answers אמן after a blessing. Here, in place of אמן, there was a call for תקיעה and תרועה, then a 'מי שענה' prayer, just like the order used in the מקדש. This sets up the question in the next step: may this ceremony be done outside the מקדש?

keyTerms.meaning: Led the prayers (literally 'passed before the ark')
The congregation's response affirming a blessing
Blow a תקיעה, a long, straight shofar sound
Blow a תרועה, a broken, wavering shofar sound
'He Who answered', the formula ending each special fast-day blessing
The mountain of the עקדה, where ה׳ answered אברהם

steps.confusionAlert: The people did not skip אמן out of carelessness. Not answering אמן was part of the מקדש's style of ceremony, which these rabbis copied in their town.

phrases.english: In the days of Rabbi Chalafta
phrases.notes: The story itself begins on the previous amud ('ומעשה').

phrases.english: and Rabbi Chananya ben Teradyon
that someone passed before the ark (led the prayer)
and finished the entire blessing,
and they did not answer 'amen' after him.
'Sound, priests, sound!'
phrases.notes: Said by the synagogue attendant, according to the גמרא's explanation.

phrases.english: He Who answered Abraham our father
on Mount Moriah,
He will answer you
and hear the voice of your cry on this day.
'Blast, sons of Aaron, blast!'

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁעָנָה אֶת אֲבוֹתֵינוּ עַל יַם סוּף,
phrases.english: He Who answered our fathers at the Red Sea,
He will answer you
and hear the voice of your cry on this day.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּימֵי רַבִּי חֲלַפְתָּא וְרַבִּי חֲנַנְיָא בֶּן תְּרַדְיוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story begun in the preceding lines of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In these rabbis' town, the fast-day blessings were done in the מקדש style: shofar blasts by כהנים and 'מי שענה' in place of אמן.

steps.title: The חכמים limit the ceremony to the מקדש
steps.stepSummary: When the חכמים heard about this practice, they said the ceremony was only done at the שער מזרח and on the הר הבית.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the matter came before the חכמים, they said: 'We only practiced this way at the שער מזרח and on the הר הבית.'
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים respond to the story. They say this ceremony belongs only in the מקדש area, not in other towns.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story showed the ceremony done outside the מקדש. The חכמים close that door: this exact order, with no אמן and with כהנים blowing between the blessings, is a מקדש practice. Doing it elsewhere is not the accepted custom.

keyTerms.meaning: When the matter reached the Sages
The Eastern Gate of the הר הבית

steps.whatToRemember: The 'no אמן + shofar + מי שענה' ceremony is a מקדש-only practice, according to the חכמים.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the general idea that some מקדש ceremonies are not copied outside it. The גמרא will later explain why אמן was not said in the מקדש.

phrases.english: And when the matter came before the Sages, they said:
We did not used to practice this way,
except at the Eastern Gate and on the Temple Mount.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Evaluates and limits the practice described in step 1.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ceremony is performed only at the שער מזרח and the הר הבית, not in outlying towns.

steps.title: רבי יהושע on how the priests fast
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה. רבי יהושע rules how strictly the אנשי משמר and the אנשי בית אב fast during each of the three sets of public fasts for rain.
steps.simpleTranslation: During the first three fasts, the men of the weekly watch fast but do not complete the fast, and the men of the day's family do not fast at all. During the second three, the watch fasts and completes it, and the day's family fasts but does not complete it. During the final seven, both groups fast and complete it. These are the words of רבי יהושע.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic starts. The משנה asks how the כהנים working in the מקדש join the community's fasts for rain, and this step gives רבי יהושע's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two groups. The אנשי משמר serve that whole week, and the אנשי בית אב are the family actually doing the service that day. The more severe the fast set, the stricter the fasting gets. In the first two sets, the day's family is one level more lenient because they are doing the actual work, but in the final seven both groups fast fully.

keyTerms.meaning: The priestly watch on duty that week
The family within the watch serving on that particular day
They complete the fast until nightfall
The final, most severe set of seven fasts

steps.confusionAlert: 'Fast but do not complete' does not mean 'do not fast.' It means they start fasting but eat before the day ends.

phrases.english: The first three fasts —
the men of the watch fast but do not complete,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַנְשֵׁי בֵּית אָב לֹא הָיוּ מִתְעַנִּין כְּלָל.
phrases.english: and the men of the patrilineal family did not fast at all.
The second three —
the men of the watch fast and complete,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַנְשֵׁי בֵּית אָב מִתְעַנִּין וְלֹא מַשְׁלִימִין.
phrases.english: and the men of the patrilineal family fast but do not complete.
The final seven —
both groups fast and complete,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehoshua.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New משנה on a new topic: the כהנים' participation in the public fasts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהושע: first three fasts, משמר partial and בית אב none; second three, משמר full and בית אב partial; final seven, both full.

steps.title: The חכמים' more lenient schedule for the כהנים
steps.stepSummary: חכמים disagree with רבי יהושע and give a more lenient schedule for the כהנים in every set of fasts.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the חכמים say: during the first three fasts, neither group fasts at all. During the second three, the watch fasts but does not complete it, and the day's family does not fast at all. During the final seven, the watch fasts and completes it, and the day's family fasts but does not complete it.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים give a competing view. It is more lenient than רבי יהושע's view, though in the final seven the משמר still fasts fully in both views.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the חכמים, the first three fasts do not touch the כהנים at all. In the final seven, the day's family still does not fully fast, while for רבי יהושע everyone fasts fully at that point. The pattern stays the same: the בית אב is always one step more lenient than the משמר.

keyTerms.meaning: And the Sages say, introducing the majority opposing view

steps.whatToRemember: In both views, fasting grows stricter with each set. For the חכמים, the בית אב is always one level more lenient than the משמר. For רבי יהושע this holds in the first two sets, but in the final seven both groups fast fully.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
The first three fasts —

phrases.aramaic: אֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ לֹא הָיוּ מִתְעַנִּין כְּלָל.
phrases.english: both groups did not fast at all.
The second three —
the men of the watch fast but do not complete,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַנְשֵׁי בֵּית אָב לֹא הָיוּ מִתְעַנִּין כְּלָל,
phrases.english: and the men of the patrilineal family did not fast at all;
the final seven —
the men of the watch fast and complete,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַנְשֵׁי בֵּית אָב מִתְעַנִּין וְלֹא מַשְׁלִימִין.
phrases.english: and the men of the patrilineal family fast but do not complete.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents the opposing view to רבי יהושע in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חכמים: first three fasts, neither group fasts; second three, משמר partial and בית אב none; final seven, משמר full and בית אב partial.

steps.title: When the priests on duty may drink wine
steps.stepSummary: The אנשי משמר may drink wine at night but not by day. The אנשי בית אב may not drink wine at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: The men of the weekly priestly shift may drink wine at night, but not during the day. The men of the family serving that day may not drink wine, day or night.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives one more difference between the whole weekly shift (משמר) and the family actually serving that day (בית אב). This time the difference is about drinking wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן who drank wine may not do the Temple service. The wider משמר might be called in by day to help, so only daytime is forbidden. The בית אב serving that day has work at night too, such as burning the leftover parts on the מזבח, so they may not drink at any time.

keyTerms.meaning: The members of the weekly priestly shift
The family within the shift that serves on a given day

phrases.english: The members of the priestly watch —
are permitted to drink wine at night,
but not during the days,
phrases.notes: By day they may be called in to help with the service.

phrases.english: and the members of the family serving that day —
neither by day nor by night.
phrases.notes: Their duties continue through the night.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַנְשֵׁי מִשְׁמָר מוּתָּרִין לִשְׁתּוֹת יַיִן בַּלֵּילוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's comparison of the משמר and the בית אב, moving from fasting to wine.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משמר: wine is allowed at night only. בית אב: no wine at all during their service.

steps.title: No haircuts or laundry during the shift week, except Thursday
steps.stepSummary: The אנשי משמר and the אנשי מעמד may not cut hair or launder during their week. On Thursday it is allowed, out of honor for שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The men of the priestly shift and the men of the מעמד may not cut their hair or wash their clothes. On Thursday they may, in honor of שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a grooming rule for the people on duty that week. This rule covers both the כהנים and the ordinary Jews of the מעמד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the אנשי מעמד, the Jews who stood beside the offerings and prayed, are included along with the כהנים. Haircuts and laundry are forbidden during the week. Thursday is the exception, so that they will look respectable for שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: The group of ordinary Jews matched to each משמר, who stood by and prayed during that week

phrases.english: The members of the priestly watch and the members of the non-priestly watch —
are forbidden to cut hair and to launder.
But on Thursday they are permitted,
because of the honor of Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַנְשֵׁי מִשְׁמָר וְאַנְשֵׁי מַעֲמָד אֲסוּרִין מִלְּסַפֵּר וּמִלְּכַבֵּס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further restriction for those on duty and widens it to include the אנשי מעמד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Haircuts and laundry are forbidden during the duty week, but allowed on Thursday for שבת.
steps.whatToRemember: This closes the משנה's rules about the people on duty: their fasting, wine, haircuts and laundry.

steps.title: Days when eulogies are forbidden: the day before is also forbidden
steps.stepSummary: On days marked in מגילת תענית as "no eulogizing," the day before is also forbidden. The day after is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Any day written in מגילת תענית as a day not to eulogize: it is forbidden the day before, and allowed the day after.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה starts a new topic. It looks at the happy days listed in מגילת תענית and asks whether the restriction also spreads to the day next to them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some days in מגילת תענית are marked "דלא למספד," meaning no eulogies. These are the more serious days of celebration. The תנא קמא says the day before is also forbidden, but the day after is not.

keyTerms.meaning: An ancient list of days of national celebration on which fasting or eulogizing is forbidden

steps.confusionAlert: Notice that the "no eulogy" days are the STRICTER days, not the lighter ones. That is why their restriction spreads further than the "no fasting" days in the next steps.

phrases.english: Any day written in Megillat Ta'anit
as "not to eulogize" —
the day before it is forbidden,
the day after it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל הַכָּתוּב בִּמְגִלַּת תַּעֲנִית דְּלָא לְמִסְפַּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new section of the משנה, about the days of מגילת תענית.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On a "no eulogy" day, the day before is forbidden too. The day after is permitted.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: both the day before and after are forbidden for eulogies
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי holds that eulogies are forbidden both the day before and the day after a "no eulogy" day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: both the day before and the day after are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי disagrees with the previous ruling and is stricter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא forbade only the day before. רבי יוסי adds the day after as well, so these serious days are protected on both sides.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who disputes several rulings in this משנה

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
both before it and after it are forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר לְפָנָיו וּלְאַחֲרָיו אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the תנא קמא of step 7 and is stricter.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eulogies are forbidden on the day before and the day after a "no eulogy" day.

steps.title: Days when fasting is forbidden: the days before and after are allowed
steps.stepSummary: On days marked "no fasting," fasting is allowed both the day before and the day after.
steps.simpleTranslation: A day marked "not to fast": fasting is permitted on the day before and on the day after.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה turns to the lighter category in מגילת תענית, the "no fasting" days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These days are less serious than the "no eulogy" days. So according to the תנא קמא, the restriction does not spread to either neighboring day.

phrases.english: A day marked "not to fast" —
the day before it and the day after it are permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the stricter "no eulogy" days to the lighter "no fasting" days.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fasting is allowed on the days before and after a "no fasting" day.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: the day before a no-fasting day is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי forbids fasting on the day before a "no fasting" day, but allows it on the day after.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: the day before is forbidden, the day after is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי again disagrees and is one step stricter than the תנא קמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Look at the pattern. For each category, רבי יוסי is exactly one level stricter. For "no fasting" days, he treats them the way the תנא קמא treated "no eulogy" days: the day before is forbidden and the day after is allowed.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
the day before it is forbidden,
the day after it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר לְפָנָיו אָסוּר לְאַחֲרָיו מוּתָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the תנא קמא of step 9 and is stricter.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fasting is forbidden on the day before a "no fasting" day and permitted on the day after.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two categories in מגילת תענית. "No eulogy" days are stricter than "no fasting" days. In both, רבי יוסי is one step stricter than the תנא קמא.

steps.title: Do not start a series of public fasts on Thursday
steps.stepSummary: A set of public fasts may not begin on a Thursday, because that would drive up prices. The first set runs Monday-Thursday-Monday. The second set runs Thursday-Monday-Thursday.
steps.simpleTranslation: We do not decree a public fast that starts on a Thursday, so as not to push up prices. Rather, the first three fasts are Monday, Thursday and Monday, and the second three are Thursday, Monday and Thursday.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה goes back to the public fasts for rain and sets which weekday they begin on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the very first fast fell on Thursday, everyone would shop on Friday for both after the fast and for שבת. Seeing the crowds, sellers would assume a famine and raise prices. Once people are already used to the fasts, the second set may begin on Thursday without causing panic.

phrases.english: We do not decree a fast on the community
starting on a Thursday,
so as not to cause prices to rise.
phrases.notes: Friday shopping crowds would lead sellers to raise prices.

phrases.english: Rather, the first three fasts are:
Monday, Thursday and Monday,
and the second three are:
Thursday, Monday and Thursday.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין גּוֹזְרִין תַּעֲנִית עַל הַצִּבּוּר בַּתְּחִילָּה בַּחֲמִישִׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new rule in the משנה about scheduling the public fasts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the first set of fasts may not start on Thursday. The second set may start on Thursday.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the חכמים weighed economic harm to the public when they set the fast schedule.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: no set of fasts begins on Thursday
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי holds that neither the second set nor the last set of fasts may begin on Thursday, just like the first.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: just as the first fasts do not start on Thursday, so too neither the second nor the last.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי disagrees with the schedule just given and applies the Thursday ban to every set of fasts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא let the second set start on Thursday. רבי יוסי says the worry about prices still applies, so every set, including the final set, starts on Monday.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
Just as the first ones are not on Thursday,
so too neither the second ones nor the last ones.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר כְּשֵׁם שֶׁאֵין הָרִאשׁוֹנוֹת בַּחֲמִישִׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the תנא קמא of step 11 and extends the Thursday ban.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every set of public fasts begins on Monday, never on Thursday.
steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא bans a Thursday start only for the first set of fasts. רבי יוסי bans it for every set.

steps.title: No public fasts on festive days
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a public fast may not be decreed on ראש חודש, חנוכה, or פורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: We do not decree a fast on the community on ראש חודש, on חנוכה, or on פורים.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a new rule: the community may not be ordered to fast on these three happy days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These days have a festive character. A public fast would clash with their joy. So the בית דין may not schedule a public fast on them.

keyTerms.meaning: the first days of the months (ראש חודש)

phrases.english: We do not decree a fast upon the community
on New Moons, on Chanukah, and on Purim.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the rule about which weekday a series of fasts may begin on to a new rule about festive days of the calendar.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A public fast may not be decreed on ראש חודש, חנוכה, or פורים.

steps.title: A series already begun is not interrupted
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל rules that if a series of fasts already began and one of them falls on such a day, the series is not stopped.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if they already started, they do not interrupt the series. These are the words of רבן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה deals with a series of fasts that started before one of these festive days. רבן גמליאל says the series keeps going.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 was about starting a new decree. This step is about a series that is already underway. רבן גמליאל holds that the fasting continues even on the festive day.

phrases.english: And if they began
they do not interrupt; these are the words of Rabban Gamliel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a case to step 13's rule: what to do when the series began before the festive day.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once a series of fasts has begun, it is not interrupted for ראש חודש, חנוכה, or פורים.

steps.title: Fasting without completing the fast
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר explains that even רבן גמליאל agrees the fast is not completed on these days. The same applies to תשעה באב on ערב שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר said: Even though רבן גמליאל said they do not interrupt, he agreed that they do not complete the fast. The same is true of תשעה באב that falls on ערב שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר limits רבן גמליאל's rule. On these days people fast, but they eat before the day ends.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a middle position. The series is not cancelled, but the fast is broken early out of respect for the day. In the same way, when תשעה באב falls on Friday, people eat before שבת so that they do not enter שבת while fasting.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'interrupting' (מפסיקין) with 'completing' (משלימין). Not interrupting means the fast day still happens. Not completing means the people eat before evening.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי מאיר, a fast that falls on ראש חודש, חנוכה, or פורים, and תשעה באב that falls on ערב שבת, is observed but not finished.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir said:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאָמַר רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אֵין מַפְסִיקִין,
phrases.english: Even though Rabban Gamliel said they do not interrupt,
he agreed that they do not complete the fast.
And likewise the Ninth of Av
that happens to fall on Friday.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאָמַר רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אֵין מַפְסִיקִין, מוֹדֶה הָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows step 14: the series continues, but the fast on these days is not completed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On these days the fast is begun but not completed, and the same is true of תשעה באב on ערב שבת.

steps.title: Is the ark ceremony done on the first fasts too?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about bringing out the ark and asks whether this happens even on the first set of fasts.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is the order of the fast days? They bring out the ark, and so on. And is this done even on the first fasts?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by quoting the earlier משנה about the ark ceremony. It then asks whether the ceremony applies even to the first fasts. This question sets up a contradiction that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה describes the ceremony without saying which fasts it applies to. That makes it sound as if it happens on every public fast. The גמרא questions that reading.

keyTerms.meaning: the Talmudic discussion of the משנה
the ark holding the Torah scrolls

phrases.english: Gemara: What is the order of the fast days?
They bring out the ark, etc.
And even on the first ones?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The משנה has ended and the גמרא now goes back to an earlier line of the משנה about the ark ceremony.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the ark-and-ashes ceremony apply to every public fast, including the first ones?

steps.title: A ברייתא limits the ceremony to the last seven fasts
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that on the first two sets of fasts people pray as usual. The ark and ashes are used only on the last seven.
steps.simpleTranslation: They pointed out a contradiction. On the first and second sets of three fasts, people enter the synagogue and pray the way they pray all year. On the last seven, they bring the ark out to the city square and put ashes on the ark, on the head of the נשיא, and on the head of the אב בית דין, and each person takes ashes and puts them on his own head. רבי נתן says: they bring burnt ashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to contradict the plain reading of the משנה. According to the ברייתא, the ark ceremony happens only on the final seven fasts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה seemed to describe the ceremony for every fast. The ברייתא clearly says the first six fasts use normal prayer in the synagogue. רבי נתן adds a detail: the ashes must be burnt ashes.

keyTerms.meaning: and they pointed out a contradiction
head of the court, deputy to the נשיא

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:
On the first and second sets of three fasts
they enter the synagogue,
and they pray in the way that they pray
the entire year.
And on the last seven

phrases.aramaic: מוֹצִיאִין אֶת הַתֵּיבָה לִרְחוֹבָהּ שֶׁל עִיר,
phrases.english: they bring the ark out to the city square,
and they place ashes on top of the ark,

phrases.aramaic: וּבְרֹאשׁ הַנָּשִׂיא, וּבְרֹאשׁ אַב בֵּית דִּין,
phrases.english: and on the head of the Nasi, and on the head of the head of the court,

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד נוֹטֵל וְנוֹתֵן בְּרֹאשׁוֹ.
phrases.english: and each and every one takes and places ashes on his own head.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי נָתָן אוֹמֵר: אֵפֶר מִקְלֶה הֵן מְבִיאִין!
phrases.english: Rabbi Natan says: They bring burnt ashes!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source behind the question in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The plain reading of the משנה, that the ark ceremony happens on every public fast.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says the first six fasts use normal prayer, and the ceremony belongs only to the last seven.

steps.title: Our משנה also means the last seven
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that our משנה was also taught only about the last seven fasts.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: When we learned our משנה too, we learned it about the last seven fasts.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא settles the contradiction by explaining that the משנה was only ever talking about the final seven fasts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no real argument between the two sources. The משנה simply left out which fasts it meant, and the ברייתא fills that in. So the ceremony belongs only to the most severe stage of fasting.
steps.whatToRemember: The ark-and-ashes ceremony is done only on the final seven fasts, not on the first two sets.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
When we learned our mishnah as well,
we learned it about the last seven.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: כִּי תְּנַן נָמֵי מַתְנִיתִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the משנה to a specific case (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to require the ceremony on every fast.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה, like the ברייתא, refers only to the last seven fasts.

steps.title: Why start the ashes with the נשיא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the order in the משנה. Ashes are a sign of shame, and רבי teaches that for shameful matters you start with the least important person.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says ashes go on the head of the נשיא, and only afterward teaches that each person puts ashes on his own head. Is that so? But it was taught in a ברייתא that רבי says: In matters of greatness we start with the greatest, and in matters of curse we start with the least.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the order in the משנה and attacks it using a rule taught by רבי. Step 20 gives the sources for רבי's rule, and step 21 answers the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting ashes on someone's head is a sign of mourning and shame, so it counts as a 'curse' matter. By רבי's rule, the least important person should go first. Yet the משנה puts the נשיא first.

keyTerms.meaning: but it was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: And on the head of the Nasi,

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲדַר תָּנֵי כׇּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד נוֹתֵן בְּרֹאשׁוֹ.
phrases.english: and then it teaches that each and every one places ashes on his head.
Is that so?!
But it was taught: Rebbi says:
In matters of greatness, we begin with the greatest,
and in matters of curse, we begin with the least.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from which fasts the ceremony applies to, to the order in which ashes are placed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's order, which places ashes on the נשיא first.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Ashes are a sign of shame, and רבי's rule is that shameful matters begin with the least important person, not the greatest.
steps.whyThisMatters: רבי's principle (greatness starts from the top, curse starts from the bottom) is a general rule used elsewhere in ש״ס.

steps.title: The verses behind the rule of who goes first
steps.stepSummary: The rule used in the challenge is backed by פסוקים. For honor, משה spoke first to אהרן, the greatest. For curses, the snake was cursed first, then חוה, then אדם.
steps.simpleTranslation: For a matter of greatness, we start with the greatest person, as it says: 'And משה said to אהרן, and to אלעזר and to איתמר.' For a curse, we start with the least important, because first the snake was cursed, then חוה was cursed, and then אדם was cursed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the challenge from step 19 by showing where רבי's rule comes from. Each half of the rule gets its own פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The honor verse lists אהרן first, before his sons, because he is the most important. The curse in גן עדן goes from the least important, the snake, up to אדם. This makes the challenge stronger: ashes are a sign of shame, so the leaders should get them last, but the משנה puts them first.

keyTerms.meaning: We start with the most important person
We start with the least important person

phrases.english: For a matter of greatness, we begin with the greatest,
as it says: 'And Moshe said to Aharon,
phrases.notes: ויקרא י:ו. The next verse speaks of the honor of the anointing oil.

phrases.english: and to Elazar and to Itamar.'
phrases.notes: The sons come after the father, who is greater.

phrases.english: And for a curse, we begin with the least important,
because first the snake was cursed,
and afterward Chava was cursed,
and afterward Adam was cursed!
phrases.notes: The exclamation shows this is still part of the challenge.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוקים for רבי's rule, which was the basis of the challenge in step 19.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that honor starts with the greatest and shame or curse starts with the least.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא י:ו for honor, and the order of the curses in גן עדן (בראשית ג) for curse.

steps.title: Going first is actually an honor for the leaders
steps.stepSummary: The leaders get the ashes first because this is a mark of honor. It is as if the people tell them: you are worthy to ask for mercy for all of us.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is an honor for them, because the people are saying to them: You are important enough to ask for mercy on behalf of everyone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Putting the leaders first is not about shame. It shows that they are the ones worthy to pray for the whole community.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that receiving ashes first is a curse-type matter, so it should start with the least important person. The answer changes how we see the act: being chosen first is an honor because the leaders represent everyone before ה׳. So the rule 'honor starts with the greatest' applies, and the משנה's order makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: To ask for mercy, meaning to pray

steps.whatToRemember: The leaders get ashes first, not as shame, but as an honor. They are the ones worthy to pray for the whole community.

phrases.english: This is an honor for them,
because the people say to them:
You are worthy
to ask for mercy on our behalf
for the whole world, meaning everyone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from steps 19 and 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing: the act is a matter of honor, not of curse.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Receiving ashes first is shameful, so it should start with the least important person.
steps.terutzMaskana: Being first is an honor that shows the leaders represent everyone in prayer, so starting with the greatest is correct.

steps.title: Why do others put ashes on the leaders' heads?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says each person puts ashes on his own head. So why don't the נשיא and the אב בית דין do the same, instead of having someone else do it for them?
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says each and every person puts ashes on his own head. Then let the נשיא and the אב בית דין also take the ashes themselves and put them on their own heads. Why is it different for them, that another person takes the ashes and puts them on their heads?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה. Then it asks why the leaders are treated differently from everyone else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone else puts ashes on himself, but the משנה says someone else puts them on the leaders. The גמרא wants to know the reason for this difference. This sets up רבי אבא's answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Puts ashes on his own head
The deputy head of the court

phrases.english: Each and every one places ashes on his head.
The Nasi and the Av Beit Din too,
let them take it themselves and place it on their heads.
What is different, that another person takes it
and places it on them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next line of the משנה and opens a new question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the leaders do not put the ashes on themselves like everyone else.

steps.title: Shaming yourself is not the same as being shamed by others
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא דמן קסרי begins to explain: a person who shames himself is not like a person who is shamed by someone else. The rest of his answer continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא from קיסרי said: A person who shames himself is not like...
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא דמן קסרי starts answering the question. The sentence is cut off here and finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that being shamed by another person is more humbling than shaming yourself. So having someone else put ashes on the leaders makes their humility greater. The full comparison comes on the next amud.
steps.confusionAlert: The sentence is not finished here. The second half, about being shamed by others, comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba of Caesarea said:
One who is humiliated by himself is not similar to...

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Being shamed by someone else is more humbling than shaming yourself, so someone else puts ashes on the leaders. The full statement continues on the next amud.
